subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Fit as a fiddle

options.text: To be in excellent health and good working order
About to buy a good musical instrument
Ready to start playing a fiddle
To have an expensive musical instrument

solution:
The correct answer is **'To be in excellent health and good working order**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fit as a fiddle** is an idiom that means to be in very good health. (बहुत अच्छे स्वास्थ्य में।)

 
 
• Example - I feel fit as a fiddle this morning.
 
 
 
• So, To be in excellent health and good working order is the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **One word substitutions** for the idiom **fit as a fiddle** include able-bodied. competent. robust. slim. strapping.
